correctness.rationale: Lanczos AV=VH+beta v_next e_last^T, Gaussian independence, Wishart integration, positive Jacobi inverse corner, and an exact rank-one resolvent pole prove the 1/T tail and iff p<1; complete-sketched regression gives the Student nu=s-k+1 comparison. Exact-rational one- and multistep checks, Gaussian-chi integral checks and numerical Student CDF checks independently corroborate intermediate formulas, not the infinite theorem.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General Gaussian regression results cover the linear coefficient distribution; the new use of the Lanczos corner-cofactor noncancellation and pole integration establishes a different nonlinear Galerkin output and universal infinite-mean consequence. No directly stronger published result covering that conclusion was identified; this is not absolute priority certification.

evidence: Sketched FOM update is inverse of a rank-one perturbed Jacobi matrix; its first-last inverse entry is always nonzero prior to Krylov termination.

Gaussian regression Student law alone is about a *linear* regression coefficient, not its singular matrix inverse; the minimal-residual comparator is exactly a regression estimator and is prior-covered.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The headline result is an implication of *combining* existing distributional regression theory with Krylov-specific irreducible Jacobi algebra and an inverse-pole integration. None of the inspected primary works draws the sharp all-k 1/T law. Given its derivation from known ingredients, literature equivalence is the principal residual originality risk.

evidence: RFOM is the sketched Petrov–Galerkin condition; Lanczos yields an inverse rank-one perturbation of a positive Jacobi matrix.
Exact complete-sketch Student regression law was identified as an ingredient, but no statement of the Galerkin pole-tail consequence was located.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Comparison includes projected Ritz zeros, inverse Student transforms, near-singular Galerkin matrices, and randomized FOM aliases. Algebraically equivalent formulas for a random reduced matrix do not themselves report the universal nonintegrability of inverse Krylov energy error. Nevertheless generic inverse-Student functionals remain an overlap risk.

value.rationale: Sharp universal oversampling-independent failure of absolute-moment integrability explains rare near-zero Ritz spikes on well-conditioned SPD systems, identifies why second-moment error estimates for unsafeguarded sketched FOM can be undefined, and separates this from sketched GMRES, whose moment threshold grows with sketch dimension. It motivates safeguards and robust tail-aware evaluation.
